COHR and LITE are reference leaders rather than alpha-discovery names; use them to validate InP device capacity, AI optical demand, and tool/material pull-through.

ALMU remains a speculative shadow candidate: the III-V-on-large-diameter-silicon thesis is relevant to InP constraints, but needs customer qualification, wafer-scale yield, and commercial AI optics revenue evidence before promotion.

The strongest near-term evidence for this node is not generic AI exposure but explicit order/backlog language around InP lasers, MOCVD/IBD/etch tools, 800G/1.6T transceivers, silicon photonics, and hyperscale data centers.

Need a follow-up search for US-listed inspection/metrology, optical test, wafer bonding, and substrate suppliers; this pass found stronger evidence in InP device leaders and Veeco equipment than in pure-play test/bonding names.

VECO should remain a priority Layer 2 candidate for the compound_photonics_tools_materials node because it has direct InP laser manufacturing equipment order evidence exceeding $250M and explicit AI optical-interconnect linkage.

AEHR is a smaller underfollowed test-equipment candidate; survival depends on proving silicon-photonics wafer-level burn-in is becoming a repeat, multi-customer revenue line rather than isolated purchase orders.
COHR can be used as a reference anchor for InP/device capacity tightness and as a read-through into upstream MOCVD, bonding, inspection, and photonics test equipment demand.

Layer 2 should verify whether US-listed access misses key non-US chokepoint suppliers such as Aixtron and Oxford Instruments; if so, consider ADR/OTC availability or use them only as non-US benchmark evidence.

VECO should be tracked as the cleanest US-listed underfollowed equipment candidate for compound-semiconductor photonics tools; key later-layer checks are backlog, MOCVD order quality, AI/InP specificity, and lead-time evidence.
AXTI should be tracked as a direct InP/GaAs substrate candidate; later layers must separate AI/datacenter optical demand from legacy telecom and assess export-control and China manufacturing risk.
ALMU should remain in the speculative_shadow lane until commercial AI datacom customer qualification, production revenue, and foundry scaling evidence improve.
COHR's InP and AI-datacom capacity commentary can serve as a reference signal for whether substrate/tool constraints are tightening or easing across the upstream optical networking stack.

US-listed universe has limited pure-play exposure to plasma etch/deposition, wafer bonding, and optical test specifically for III-V/CPO; future passes should search MKSI, ONTO, CAMT, AEIS, TER, KEYS, and foreign-listed Aixtron/Oxford Instruments as comparables or secondary mappings.
AIXTRON and Oxford Instruments are credible upstream photonics-tool reference names for the AI optics / compound-semiconductor chokepoint lane.
Aeluma belongs only in a speculative shadow bucket until customer, revenue, and production evidence confirm meaningful AI-photonics exposure.

The market likely under-tags upstream photonics equipment and process-tool suppliers as AI beneficiaries because they are often classified as industrial/scientific instruments rather than AI infrastructure.
